searches.reason: Explore whether learned relative-time and recency biases inside a single BERT4Rec can distinguish recent repeated interests from older isolated interactions. Prioritize lightweight mechanisms using observed timestamps, preserving bidirectional masked-target learning and appended-mask inference; historical interactions do not establish continuing demand.

searches.reason: Investigate jointly trained item representations that capture specific textual connections beyond broad topic similarity. Seek practical title/description encoders trained from scratch within one BERT4Rec, with target content hidden at masked positions and no external pretrained weights or separately fitted scoring model. Titles may provide compatibility clues but cannot establish ownership or exact suitability.

searches.reason: Challenge the assumption that improving individual positive-negative margins sufficiently improves top-10 ranking. Seek candidate-set or differentiable ranking objectives suitable for one masked bidirectional Transformer, examining false-negative robustness and computational cost. The current training margins motivate investigation but do not establish validation ranking quality; compare alternatives using the unchanged host macro HR@10.
